Diclofenac, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), is causally associated with Purpuric Rash, which is linked to Ketoprofen, another NSAID. Ketoprofen binds to Slc22a11, a gene implicated in the transport of monocarboxylic acids across cell membranes. This suggests that the observed relationship between Diclofenac and Slc22a11 may be mediated through a shared pathway involving NSAIDs and their interaction with Slc22a11. The evidence supports a plausible mechanism where NSAIDs may influence Slc22a11 function, potentially through the transport of monocarboxylic acids, which could have implications for cellular homeostasis and inflammatory responses. The connection is supported by the presence of a common ancestor in the NSAID class, reinforcing the biological relevance of the observed relationship.
